Quinine (usually as quinine sulfate or bisulfate) has traditionally been used for nocturnal cramps (p.1887) but there has been concern over its efficacy and potential for adverse effects, especially in the elderly. In the USA, for example, the FDA ruled that quinine products should no longer be used for the management of nocturnal cramps.1,2 A similar ban has been im- posed in Australia.3 Meta-analyses4,5 concluded that although quinine was effective in the treatment of nocturnal cramps in am- bulatory patients the risk of serious adverse effects should be borne in mind.
